recommendation: Keep the source fix as-is. It is a narrow correction to the FHIR-49675 application and no further core-source work is recommended for this issue.
issue_request: FHIR-49675 was Applied/Persuasive with Modification for R6. It asked ImagingStudy to stop treating accession number as an ImagingStudy.identifier and instead describe accession numbers on ImagingStudy.basedOn by using Reference.identifier with identifier.type ACSN, with matching search-parameter wording.
initial_application: Commit 1386be9f55 applied the issue by removing accession-number language from ImagingStudy.identifier, adding accession-number requirements and aliasing to ImagingStudy.basedOn, moving search-parameter descriptions, and changing the narrative example. The structured source reflected the intended model, but the example reintroduced an invalid extra reference object level previously corrected by FHIR-41484.
additional_context: FHIR-48644 is the earlier applied decision that placed accession number on ImagingStudy.identifier, and FHIR-49675 reversed that location after identifier-scope discussion in FHIR-48692. FHIR-56033 later removed another ImagingStudy.identifier accession-number comment. FHIR-41484 specifically corrected the same erroneous reference wrapper in the basedOn accession-number example.
reconciliation: Updated source/imagingstudy/imagingstudy-notes.xml so the accession-number example is a valid ImagingStudy.basedOn Reference object whose identifier carries ACSN directly. No structuredefinition or search-parameter edits were needed because those sources already implement the FHIR-49675 basedOn model.
source_changes: source/imagingstudy/imagingstudy-notes.xml: removed the non-existent reference wrapper from the basedOn accession-number JSON example.
